title.narrative: WB Zimbabwe Socio Economic Transformation Fund (ZISET)
WB Zimbabwe Socio Economic Transformation Fund (ZISET)

description.narrative:
The ZISET TF will support the implementation of the World Bank Group´s new Country Engagement Note FY25-26 which is structured around four objectives:
(1) Reduce macroeconomic distortions and strengthen fiscal policy and economic governance,
(2) Strengthen the enabling environment for an inclusive and resilient private sector,
(3) Boost pro-poor social services and women´s empowerment, and
(4) Promote energy transition and resilience to climate change and disasters.
The specific development objective of ZISET TF is to promote inclusive growth and socio-economic resilience. The focus is on strengthening the conditions for citizens and private sector firms to benefit from and be resilient to shifts in a developing macroeconomic environment, as well as to withstand shocks, including those linked to climate change. The TF aims at supporting policy development and reforms to improve the enabling environment for private sector led economic growth, trade, and job creation, as we all as contribute to strengthening the systems for social protection for the poorest and most vulnerable.
ZISET activities are organized under two pillars, with inclusion of underserved groups, such as women, girls and the extreme poor as a cross-cutting priority, to tackle social exclusion and fragmentation.
Pillar 1. Supporting inclusive, private sector-led growth
Activities under this pillar will promote economic transformation and creation of quality jobs by strengthening the private sector enabling environment, enhancing firm capabilities and competitiveness, facilitating cross-border trade, and promoting financial sector resilience and inclusion. Supporting women-led businesses and addressing gender gaps in economic opportunities will be prioritized across intervention areas, including the selection of value-chains with high concentration of women entrepreneurs, active engagement with women-led business associations, and tailoring of interventions to account for women´s reduced mobility and higher caring responsibilities.
Key expected outcomes include:
(1) Lower costs and streamlined licensing and compliance requirements for private sector, particularly in priority sectors.
(2) Improved firm-level practices, enhancing productivity and competitiveness
(3) Streamlined and lower cost of cross-border trade clearance procedures and systems Improved access to finance
(4) Increased adoption of climate risk financial instruments
(5) Strengthen and operationalize a new Green Industrial Policy
Pillar 2. Building household resilience and womens inclusion
Pillar 2 aims to bolster the resilience of the poorest and most vulnerable households and populations by improving the targeting, coordination, and resilience of social programs. Focus areas include strengthening and improving the targeting system for social protection programs by designing and operationalizing a social registry system and expanding the registry´s coverage to 20 percent of the population. Improving the shock-responsiveness of social protection programs and designing an improved the targeting system based on poverty and vulnerability data is also foreseen. In addition, activities will promote positioning of the social registry as a service platform across sectors, programs and financing sources to enhance harmonization and coordination in the sector.
Key expected outcomes include:
(1) Strengthening the Government of Zimbabwe capacity for implementation of the social protection system
(2) Enhanced coverage of the social protection system
(3) Improved shock-responsiveness of the social protection programs
Depending on available funding to the TF, the ZISET also proposes to work on improving the design of and to pilot cash programs aimed at adolescent girls, as well as support activities that specifically target women micro-entrepreneurs to increase productivity, financial resilience and earnings.

Målet med multigivarfonden är att bidra til ekonomisk stabilitet och inkluderande tillväxt i Zimbabwe genom att stärka den privata sektorn för ökat jobbskapande, förbättra offentlig förvaltning samt öka samhällets motståndskraft.

The objective of the trust-fund is to promote economic stability and inclusive growth in Zimbabwe by strengthening the private sector to create jobs, improving public sector effectiveness and building climate resilience.

1. Business Environment Reform: reduced burdens and stronger regulatory systems
Substantial progress has been made toward strengthening the enabling environment for private-sector led growth. Three major reform action plans in the beef, dairy and feedstock sectors were finalized and approved by Cabinet, directly reducing costs, duplications and compliance burdens, thereby supporting Objectives 1 and 2 of the program. These reforms have improved transparency and contributed to a more predictable regulatory landscape. They are also expected to particularly benefit women-led micro and small enterprises, which typically face higher regulatory barriers and mobility constraints. In addition, the reforms contribute to a more climate-resilient private sector by easing regulatory constraints that limit investment in climate-adaptive production and technologies. Institutional capacity has increased as well, with more than ten ministries and agencies trained in regulatory analysis, licensing reform and compliance-cost modelling.
- Cabinet-approved reforms reducing fees, permits and regulatory steps
- Compliance databases and cost models established for priority sectors
- Multi-agency capacity building completed
- Cross-border trade study for Victoria FallsLivingstone informing tourism and trade reforms
2. Competitiveness and Access to Finance: foundations for enterprise growth
Progress under this component has strengthened the conditions for inclusive private-sector growth. A large-scale horticulture BDS program, expected to reach at least 5,000 hubs and farmers, is being prepared to enhance firm-level practices, productivity and access to markets. Diagnostics on MSME bankability and SACCOs are informing future reforms to improve access to finance, while a digital finance pilot has been co-developed with regulators and fintechs.
- BDS framework prepared for 5,000 horticulture actors
- MSME bankability and SACCO diagnostics underway
- Digital finance pilot designed; correspondent banking conference planned
3. Social Protection Systems: strengthened targeting and program design
Significant advancements have been made toward strengthening the Governments capacity to deliver inclusive and shock-responsive social protection, in alignment with Objective 3. The ZISO harmonized questionnaire was piloted, validated, and finalized, preparing the groundwork for nationwide enumeration. Governments co-financing commitment for ZISO IT hosting demonstrates growing ownership. Furthermore, the new Zimbabwe Social Cash Transfer (ZSCT) has been designed to harmonize fragmented programmes and improve targeting. Work has also progressed on vulnerability assessment and the redesign of BEAM, including a cash-plus pilot for adolescent girls. These efforts collectively enhance the systems ability to respond to climate-related shocks while improving access to services for women, girls and other under-served groups.
- Harmonized questionnaire finalized; population-level enumeration prepared
- Government co-financing secured for ZISO IT upgrades
- ZSCT program designed with improved targeting
- Vulnerability assessment drafted; BEAM redesign initiated
Unexpected results
- The Victoria Falls-Livingstone study catalyzed new Zambia-Zimbabwe dialogue, opening opportunities for cross-border tourism and trade cooperation.
- Government began co-financing ZISO IT support earlier than anticipated, signalling stronger national ownership and improving sustainability.
- Presidential engagement significantly raised the visibility of business-environment reforms, helping to accelerate national momentum for regulatory simplification and creating favourable conditions for sustaining gender- and climate-responsive reforms beyond Sida's support.
Interim Results as at August 2025
Summary of Implementation Progress The results provided in this section emanate from the August 2025 Interim annual report which provided an overview of the progress made on activities financed by the Zimbabwe Socio-Economic Transformation Fund (ZISET). The interim report received from the WB covered its full year of implementation, with Sweden having joined in December of 2024. It highlights significant progress made in, i) supporting the development of policy and regulatory reforms to address bottlenecks in the business environment, and ii) preparing to roll out mass enumeration exercise using the Social Registry Harmonized Questionnaire, which will cover two percent of Zimbabwe's population to progressively expand coverage of the Zimbabwe Social Registry (ZISO).
Pillar 1. Supporting inclusive, private sector-led growth - Three reform action plans for beef, dairy, and feedstock were completed and approved by the Cabinet, while work is underway to finalize reforms for the tourism sector. These reforms will reduce the stock of regulatory requirements (and associated costs) for the three value chains. Technical assistance (TA) provided analytical evidence to the Office of the President and Cabinet (OPC)-led ease of doing business initiative through comprehensive analysis of sector-level regulatory requirements, the development of reform action plans, and capacity building for relevant regulatory authorities. This has received considerable presidential and media attention. Over ten institutions participated in workshops to support these efforts, helping to drive momentum for future sectoral reforms. Looking ahead, discussions are ongoing to engage consultants for similar sector analyses in horticulture. Consultations with the OPC and the Ministry of Finance, Economic Development and Investment Promotion (MoFEDIP) are helping determine priorities for upcoming sectors, with cotton, fertilizer, and fisheries under consideration.
- A comprehensive study assessing the Victoria Falls-Livingstone border from both Zimbabwe and Zambia context to inform reforms was completed. The assessment, shared with the Ministry of Tourism and Hospitality Industry (MOTHI), proposes reform recommendations based on best practices and case studies. Presentations outlining trade and tourism challenges and opportunities were also made to the Zimbabwe Trade Development and Promotion Organization (ZimTrade) and MOTHI, providing actionable guidance for reform.
- Technical assistance to support competitiveness, entrepreneurship, and access to finance is underway. To promote firms competitiveness and entrepreneurship, work is ongoing to onboard a service provider for business development services (BDS) to develop and deliver a diagnostic and capacity-building framework to at least 5,000 horticulture hubs and farmers. This framework will cover critical topics such as food safety certifications, market requirements, climate-smart practices, and financing options.
- To improve access to finance and digital financial services, diagnostics on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) bankability and Savings and Credit Cooperative Organizations (SACCOs) are underway. Specifically, at the request of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, a diagnostic assessment on the SACCO sector was initiated to address data and regulatory gaps affecting their role in financial inclusion. A pilot to test the use of digital financial services for SMEs financing was launched, developed in collaboration with local Fintech companies and financial sector regulators. Planning for a correspondent banking conference is also underway.
- Technical review and inputs were provided on the first framework for the National Industrial Development Strategy 2 (NIDS 2). Technical sessions were held at the request from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MoIC) on good practices in industrial policy development, drawing on examples from regional and comparative countries.
Pillar 2. Building household resilience and women's inclusion
- Pre-testing and adoption of the Social Registry Harmonized Questionnaire. The Social Registry Harmonized Questionnaire, developed through WBG technical assistance, was piloted in Gweru district, where 80 households were surveyed. Following the pilot, the questionnaire was finalized and validated by the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare (MPSLSW) during a workshop with key stakeholders. An agreement was reached with the Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (ZIMSTAT) to conduct the first wave of enumeration, which will cover two percent of the population, starting in three selected districts. Procurement for this activity is currently underway.
- Development of the Zimbabwe Social Cash Transfer (ZSCT) program. Support was provided to the MPSLSW in collaboration with UNICEF for the development of the Zimbabwe Social Cash Transfer (ZSCT) program. The ZSCT consolidates the former Harmonized Social Cash Transfer (HSCT) and Monthly Maintenance Allowance (MMA) programs, aiming to reduce duplication and improve targeting through the use of ZISO. Technical assistance included drafting an operational manual, which has been shared with MPSLSW, other government stakeholders, and development partners for review and input. The manual is expected to be adopted soon by MPSLSW.
- Reinforcing resilience and crisis response. Progress has been made in strengthening resilience and crisis response mechanisms. A draft vulnerability assessment has been prepared to inform crisis response programming. After incorporation of household data expected soon from ZIMSTAT, the draft assessment will be shared with government and partners for discussion prior to finalization. However, the preparation of a crisis response manual has been postponed at the MPSLSWs request until the completion of the National Social Protection Strategy.
- Advancing social services for adolescent girls and women. Efforts to improve adolescent girls access to social services have progressed, with priorities for redesigning the Basic Education Assistance Module (BEAM) program identified and a concept note for a cash-plus pilot linking BEAM beneficiaries to social services submitted to the MPSLSW. Recruitment for a consultant to update the BEAM operational manual is underway.
Reference: Klaradia UM2024/02424/HARA/50- WB ZISET Interim Report Aug 2025
